changes: p1 Viśveśvara: confidence lowered to medium; the title in parentheses is garbled, so his exact role (commentator or author of a gloss) is uncertain
p2: as_written widened to include the '-jī' honorific. The name stays Raṇachoḍa and the residence stays as given
p3 Śāma: residence removed. The colophon gives residence only for the scribe, so it should not be carried over to the father. The caste affiliation is kept because it is inherited

date: ce_approx changed from 1823 to 1824. In Gujarat (Junagadh) VS years start in Kārttika, so Āṣāḍha śukla 15 of VS 1880 falls in mid-1824. The full moon of about 11 July 1824 was a Sunday, which matches 'ravau dine'. The Caitrādi alternative, about 23 July 1823, was a Wednesday
date: tithi normalised to pūrṇimā and weekday to Sunday (ravau dine)
place: emptied. 'jīrṇadurga nivāsi' gives the scribe's residence, not the place of copying. Copying at Junagadh is likely but not stated (see notes)

persons.name: Raṇachoḍa
persons.evidence: lī o. bhaṭa raṇachoḍajī śāmajī śrīgoḍajñātīya || śrījīrṇadurga nivāsi

notes: 'lī o.' probably abbreviates likhitam. Raṇachoḍajī Śāmajī follows the Gujarati pattern of personal name + father's name, both with the honorific -jī; Śāma may stand for Śyāma. The scribe was a Bhaṭṭa of the Śrīgauḍa jñāti living in Jīrṇadurga (Junagadh, Gujarat). The catalogue gives 'Jīrṇadurganivāsī' as the place of copying, but the colophon describes it as the scribe's residence; copying there is likely but not stated. The title passage '(aṣṭavakraviśveśvaraviracitāyāṣṭāvakrakālasaṃkramaṇāddivyākhyā)' is corrupt (the cataloguer flags it with note 1). Viśveśvara seems to be named as the author of a commentary or gloss (vyākhyā), but the reading is uncertain. Date check: in western India VS years start in Kārttika, so Āṣāḍha śukla 15 of VS 1880 falls on about 11 July 1824, a Sunday, matching the colophon. The Caitrādi reading (about 23 July 1823) would fall on a Wednesday.
